editorNote: Two large open-weight models, one Nobel for ice-bound neutrino hunting, and a few results with honest caveats: agents proposing materials that nobody has made yet, and a training method that works but can't compete with backprop.

stories.headline: Mistral Large 4: 1.05T-parameter open-weight multimodal model with 1M-token context, in public preview
stories.summary: Mistral's docs list 1.05T total and 49B active parameters in a mixture-of-experts design with a 1.6B vision encoder. API pricing is $0.68 per million input tokens and $2.09 per million output.
stories.whyItMatters: It adds a very large open-weight model with long context and function calling at a published per-token price.

stories.headline: Reflection announces Beam, a 501B open-weight model; weights due later this month
stories.summary: Beam is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 23B active parameters, which Reflection says scores 80.9% on SWE-Bench Verified and 90.5% on GPQA Diamond. It remains in final red-teaming; Apache 2.0 weights are promised for later in October.
stories.whyItMatters: The benchmark figures are the company's own and the weights are not yet out, so nothing is independently checkable yet.

stories.headline: Francis Halzen wins the Nobel Prize in Physics for IceCube and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
stories.summary: The prize recognises Halzen's decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice finished in 2011. IceCube reported 28 extra-solar neutrinos in 2013 and in 2018 traced one to a blazar about 3.7 billion light-years away.
stories.whyItMatters: The award confirms neutrino astronomy as an established way to observe extreme cosmic sources.

stories.headline: Vals reports Opus 5.5 agents proposed two room-temperature magnetic semiconductor candidates, with no lab measurements yet
stories.summary: Agents ran density-functional-theory simulations to design YBaMnFeO₅ (predicted 2.35 eV gap, ordering near 420 K) and to flag KV[Cr(CN)₆], synthesised in 1999 with ordering up to 376 K. The write-up says neither gap nor spin sorting has been measured, and the first compound may be hard to make.
stories.whyItMatters: These are computational predictions for a perfect, dry crystal; real samples may differ, so the claim awaits experiment.

stories.headline: Dust trains transformer language models without backpropagation by perturbing activations at every token
stories.summary: The zeroth-order method treats each token as a virtual population member, and the authors report it needs 1,000–10,000× less population than the weight-space method EGGROLL. At large populations it approaches or exceeds backprop on their pretraining runs of 10M–20M tokens.
stories.whyItMatters: The authors say plainly it is not compute-efficient enough to replace backprop today; the result is about scaling behaviour, not a replacement.

sourceLinks.title: Dust: Pretraining Transformers Without Backpropagation - qlabs

stories.headline: Polars 2.0 makes the streaming engine the default and breaks row-order guarantees
stories.summary: LazyFrame.collect() now uses the streaming engine, which does not guarantee row order for joins, group_by and unpivot unless maintain_order=True is set. The release also enables spill-to-disk by default (from about 80% RAM), adds a native Map type, and reports leading DataFusion and DuckDB on TPC-H and TPC-DS.
stories.whyItMatters: Code that relied on implicit row order can silently change output after upgrading, which is why this is a major version.
